questions.question: Q: How did Socrates differ from the Sophists?
questions.correctAnswer: Socrates sought truth through questioning (dialectic) and did not charge fees. The Sophists taught rhetoric and persuasion for pay, claiming to make the weaker argument appear stronger. Socrates criticised the Sophists for teaching persuasion without concern for truth or morality.

questions.question: Q: What was the Socratic method?
questions.correctAnswer: Socrates asked a series of probing questions that exposed contradictions in his interlocutor's beliefs. By showing that confident claims were actually ill-founded, he aimed to lead people toward genuine knowledge. He claimed to know only that he knew nothing (Socratic ignorance).

questions.question: Q: Why was Socrates put on trial?
questions.correctAnswer: In 399 BC, Socrates was charged with impiety (not recognising the city's gods) and corrupting the youth. His questioning had embarrassed powerful Athenians, and he was associated (unfairly) with Critias, a leader of the brutal oligarchy of the Thirty Tyrants. His trial reflected anxiety about threats to democratic values after the trauma of the Peloponnesian War.

questions.question: Q: What was Plato's contribution to philosophy?
questions.correctAnswer: Plato preserved Socratic ideas through his dialogues and developed original philosophy including the Theory of Forms (that perfect, eternal ideas exist beyond the physical world). He founded the Academy, the first institution of higher learning in the Western world, and wrote influential works including the Republic on justice and ideal government.

questions.question: Q: Why was Athens a centre for philosophy and intellectual life?
questions.correctAnswer: Athens' democracy encouraged open debate and free speech (parrhesia). Its wealth, cosmopolitan population and cultural confidence attracted thinkers from across the Greek world. The agora and symposia provided venues for discussion. Athenian imperialism brought wealth that supported leisure for philosophical activity.
